questions.prompt: What do all the threads of a process share?
questions.explain: Each thread has its own stack and registers; everything else belongs to the process.
option_notes: False: every thread has its own stack.

questions.prompt: What does each thread have of its own?
options: Its own program counter, registers and stack
questions.explain: A thread needs its own point of execution and its own local variables, so it has its own registers and stack.
Threads share the global `x`, so the main thread sees the change once the thread has finished.
`pthread_join` hands back the pointer the thread returned.

questions.prompt: Why is `pthread_create(&t[i], NULL, f, &i)` inside a `for` loop a bug?
options: All threads receive the address of the same variable, which keeps changing
Threads cannot be created in loops
questions.explain: Give each thread its own argument (for example `&ids[i]` from an array).

questions.prompt: What is the type of the function that a thread runs?
questions.explain: It takes one `void *` (your data) and returns a `void *` (the result for `pthread_join`).

questions.prompt: A program that uses pthreads is compiled with the option -{{0}}.
questions.explain: `-pthread` is the recommended form (the slides write `-lpthread`).

questions.prompt: A thread returns the address of one of its own local variables. What is wrong?
options: The variable no longer exists after the thread ends
questions.explain: A thread's stack is gone when it ends. Return a `malloc`ed block or fill a struct that belongs to the caller.

options: Waits for a thread to end and can collect its result
questions.explain: It is the thread equivalent of `waitpid`.

options: The threads of a process are scheduled independently
A thread can end simply by returning from its function
When `main` returns, the other threads keep running
A thread can only end by calling `pthread_exit`
questions.explain: A `return` from the thread function is equivalent to `pthread_exit` (the slides say threads "always" end with it; they do not need to). When `main` returns, the whole process ends.
option_notes: False: the process ends and takes all its threads with it.

questions.prompt: `main` returns while other threads are still running. What happens?
options: The whole process ends, killing them
They are moved to another process
questions.explain: Returning from `main` calls `exit`. Join the threads you need, or end `main` with `pthread_exit`.
